title: doctor's binary_freshness compares the real release version and watches the manifest that carries it
action:
The binary_freshness row is blind on BOTH arms, and it answered ok while the installed binary was a whole release behind its checkout (a 2.17.1 binary in a 2.18.0 tree, on 2026-08-21, with bee status reporting onboarding.drift true at the same moment). Arm one, the version comparison in binary_freshness_row: source_version comes from parse_workspace_version over packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml and installed_version comes from the probed binary's rs-info `version`, which is env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION") — the SAME pinned workspace value. Both are 0.1.0 and no release ever bumps either, so the two operands cannot disagree and the branch is dead code that reports agreement with authority. The real release version is BEE_VERSION, extracted at compile time in version.rs from .claude-plugin/plugin.json. Arm two, source_inputs(): it walks packages/bee-rs/crates for .rs and Cargo.toml, adds the workspace Cargo.toml, and adds packages/bee/prompts/*.md — but never .claude-plugin/plugin.json, which version.rs include_str!s and is therefore a genuine compile-time input. A release bump touches only that manifest, so the mtime arm cannot see a release bump either.

Change, in three parts. (1) rs_info() in router.rs gains a `bee_version` field carrying crate::version::BEE_VERSION beside the existing `version` field; leave `version` in place — it is CARGO_PKG_VERSION and other readers may depend on it. (2) binary_freshness_row reads the source release version from <root>/.claude-plugin/plugin.json (a small runtime read of the same file version.rs embeds — serde_json is already a dependency; do not try to reuse the const fn, it parses the manifest embedded in THIS binary, not the one in the checkout under test) and compares it against the probed binary's `bee_version`. Keep packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml as the marker that makes the row exist at all — that gate is what keeps a host project from ever seeing this row — but stop using its version as an operand. A probed binary that answers rs-info WITHOUT a bee_version field is itself stale: it predates this change, so report not_ok naming that, never fall through to ok. A missing or unreadable .claude-plugin/plugin.json in a tree that does have the workspace Cargo.toml reports unknown rather than ok — never invent agreement from a file it could not read. (3) add .claude-plugin/plugin.json to source_inputs() so the mtime arm catches a bump even when the version arm cannot probe.

Tests, in doctor/tests.rs. The source_checkout fixture must now also write a .claude-plugin/plugin.json carrying the release version, so give it that version as its own parameter rather than reusing workspace_version — the whole point is that the two are different values. write_executable_binary's stub script must answer both fields. Rewrite binary_freshness_reports_not_ok_on_a_version_mismatch so the mismatch is a RELEASE version mismatch (manifest says one thing, binary's bee_version says another) with every mtime older than the binary, which is precisely the case the old assertion could never have caught. Keep binary_freshness_is_ok_when_matched_and_newest green with matching release versions. Add: a manifest newer than the binary is not_ok and the detail names .claude-plugin/plugin.json; a binary whose rs-info omits bee_version is not_ok; a checkout with no .claude-plugin/plugin.json is unknown, not ok. Add one regression test that pins the real defect directly — a binary and a workspace Cargo.toml that agree on the pinned package version while the release versions differ must be not_ok, so the tautology can never come back. The unknown-without-a-binary and absent-outside-a-source-checkout tests stay as they are.

The remedy text in REMEDY already names the right command; leave it. Do not touch version.rs, the const fn, or the two plugin manifests.

truths: The version arm compares the checkout's release version against the release version the installed binary reports, never two copies of the pinned package version
A binary one release behind its checkout is reported not_ok even when every source mtime is older than it
A binary too old to report its release version is not_ok, never ok
A checkout whose plugin manifest cannot be read is unknown, never ok
The mtime arm treats the plugin manifest as a source input
A host project with no workspace Cargo.toml still never carries this row

artifacts.substantive: release-version comparison replacing the workspace-version one, the manifest added to source_inputs, and the unknown and too-old arms; no TODO stubs
rs-info answers bee_version beside the existing version field

fixture writes a plugin manifest with its own version, the mismatch test rewritten to a release mismatch, plus the new manifest-mtime, missing-bee_version, unreadable-manifest and tautology-regression cases

key_links: a check whose two operands are the same constant answers ok with authority and is worse than no check
prohibitions: No change to version.rs, its const fn, or either plugin manifest
The existing rs-info `version` field is not removed or repurposed
packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml stays the marker that gates the row's existence
No process spawned in any test beyond the existing executable stub
